ancestry_summary.statement_nl: Let $n$ be an integer greater than 1. For which real numbers $x$ is \\[\\lfloor nx \\rfloor - \\sum_{k=1}^{n} \\frac{\\lfloor kx \\rfloor}{k}\\] maximal, and what is the maximal value that this expression can take?

payload.proof_nl: Let x be any real number. By the defining property of the floor function, floor(x) is an integer with floor(x) ≤ x. Subtracting floor(x) from both sides gives 0 ≤ x - floor(x). Since x was arbitrary, this holds for every real number x. Hence, for all real x, 0 ≤ x - floor(x).
payload.role_in_assembly: Supplies the lower-bound part of the fractional-part estimate before rewriting the difference as frac(x).
